newsitem.title: USA: IBM launches electronic commerce products.
newsitem.headline: IBM launches electronic commerce products.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. on Wednesday introduced electronic commerce technologies aimed at making itself a one-stop shop for doing business on the Internet's World Wide Web.
The package of electronic commerce products and services, dubbed CommercePoint, is designed to provide buying and selling over the multimedia portion of the Internet.

"The opportunity here goes beyond forging transactions on the Internet," Dr. Irving Wladawsky-Berger, general manager of IBM's Internt Division, told reporters at a news conference in a downtown San Francisco hotel.
IBM said its complete end-to-end services product would be based on a monthly fee, or individual applications could be purchased a la carte as businesses purchase and install them.
The company said its CommercePoint initiative would "the most complete and secure infrastructure" for credit and debit card transactions.

The company said customers such as mail order outfitter L.L. Bean were already developing some 40 "smart catalogus" which are displayed electronically and can continually rearranged based on customers' preferences.
IBM said it was offering three types of CommercePoint services and products.
"The three variations let retailers go it alone, provide some handholding from IBM or offer a complete outsourcing arrangement," the company said in a statement.
Net.Commerce will be for businesses "which need to reach customers in tempting new ways." IBM said it will be available worldwide from the fourth quarter starting at $5,000.

IBM also announced World Avenue, an on-line Web "mall" offering a secure way to sell goods and services to millions of customers, and World Commerce, for businesses that want a private, stand-alone merchant site without having to create and manage it.
